summary: HTTP/2 stream reordering + LB write-queue backpressure during multipart embedding uploads causing 504s
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports recurring 504s for long embedding batch uploads using multipart/form-data over HTTP/2. Failures began after increased adoption of a client-side batching flow that uploads many small files (per-item embeddings) in a single connection.

Impact:
- Multiple customers (starting with LumenHealth dedicated cluster) see ~15-30% of embedding requests end with 504 Gateway Timeout when upload size > ~8MB total and when client uses HTTP/2 multiplexing.
- Affects embedding throughput and increases user-visible latency for downstream features (search and semantic matching).

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster for LumenHealth (prod-us-west).
- API traffic via our public API gateway terminating TLS and proxying to internal ALBs and nginx sidecars on serving nodes.
- Client uses HTTP/2 with multiplexed streams and periodic TLS session ticket renewals.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Use client that batches 200 small items (avg 40KB each) and sends as multipart/form-data over a single HTTP/2 connection.
2) Start continuous uploads at ~12 concurrent connections.
3) Observe occasional 504s after ~10–30s into the request; request body upload completed from client perspective but server returns 504.

Observed logs / telemetry snippets:
- api-gateway: "upstream response timeout while reading upstream" with upstream addr pointing to internal ALB.
- alb-metrics: increased ActiveConnectionDrain and WriteQueueDepth spikes on target group during incidents.
- nginx-sidecar: long stall on proxy_send() followed by "connection reset by peer".
- tcpdump (customer pcap): retransmits and delayed ACKs clustered around TLS session ticket renewal timestamps.

Initial hypothesis:
- HTTP/2 multiplexing combined with TLS ticket rotation and ALB write-queue head-of-line blocking is causing per-connection write stalls. Small multipart chunks are coalesced then hit a limited write window on the ALB/NGINX side, which blocks application reads until the socket becomes writable. When the ALB's idle/write timeout crosses our proxy idle threshold, gateway returns 504 even though client had finished uploading.

Why this is unusual / different from other timeout tickets:
- Not simple header bloat or single huge header; this is driven by many small bodies + HTTP/2 stream scheduling + occasional TLS ticket events that correlate with write-queue reordering. Existing tickets focus on header growth or ALB idle timeouts; here we see scheduling-induced stalls on the write path even when aggregate throughput is under expected limits.
investigation_notes: 03/10 09:40 - Reproduced in staging by replaying customer's request pattern against dedicated staging cluster. Observed write queue depth spikes on ALB and nginx when client used HTTP/2 multiplexing.
03/10 11:15 - Disabled HTTP/2 on ingress in staging: issue frequency dropped to <1%. Suggests HTTP/2 stream behavior contributes to the problem.

03/10 14:30 - Correlated TLS session ticket rotation (server-side) with clustered retransmits in pcap. Hypothesis: ticket rotation briefly delays TLS write completion which interacts badly with our internal socket write buffering.
03/11 08:20 - Captured nginx debug logs showing proxy_send() returning EWOULDBLOCK for several seconds; application/serving-runtime waits on socket writable and then times out upstream read.

03/11 13:05 - Checked ALB configuration: idle timeout set to 60s (default), but observed internal proxy idle timeouts of 30s in some nodes due to earlier experimental config. Inconsistent timeouts increase race surface.

03/11 16:10 - Hypothesis refined: combination of (a) HTTP/2 multiplexing coalescing writes into bursts, (b) occasional TLS ticket renewals or session resumption events causing transient stalls, and (c) misaligned internal idle/write timeouts across the proxy stack leads to 504s even though client upload succeeded.

comments: Ava Thompson (03/10): Customer reported new failures after their latest client rollout. Provided pcap and request samples. Asked for priority triage.
Mateo Ruiz (03/10): Assigned for triage. Requested staging reproduction and debug logs. Spun up dedicated staging cluster and ran client's replay script.
SRE - Priya Kaur (03/11): Confirmed write-queue spikes on ALB during replay. Recommends aligning proxy and ALB idle timeouts and testing with HTTP/1.1 fallback to validate hypothesis.

Eng - Dan Vogel (03/11): Noted an existing nginx tuning PR that reduced proxy_send buffer size in some nodes (rolled out 2026-02-25). Investigating if heterogeneous config is present across the fleet.
next_steps: 1) Roll back the nginx proxy buffer-size change on a subset of staging nodes to ensure homogeneous behavior across cluster (Mateo) - target 2026-03-12.
2) Align ALB and internal proxy idle/write timeouts (set both to 90s) for LumenHealth dedicated cluster and monitor for 24h (SRE team) - target 2026-03-12.

3) Add temporary gate: if client Content-Type is multipart/form-data and connection uses HTTP/2, prefer HTTP/1.1 backend proxying for this customer's VPN (short-term mitigation) - product engineering to approve.

4) Long-term: implement write-side backpressure metrics and increase ALB write-socket buffer sizing; add test to our chaos suite to exercise TLS ticket rotation under high multiplexed HTTP/2 load (platform).
resolution: (in progress) Temporary mitigation deployed to LumenHealth dedicated cluster: forced backend proxying to HTTP/1.1 for multipart uploads coming from their CIDR. Early telemetry shows error rate dropped from 18% -> 2% for the replayed workload. Follow-up actions include full-batch alignment of timeouts and a config rollback test in staging. Final fix will require coordinated nginx buffer and ALB tuning plus adding targeted tests to our regression suite.
resolution_notes: 03/12 - Mitigation applied: customer CIDR rule to downgrade HTTP/2 multiplexing to HTTP/1.1 at ingress for multipart uploads. Monitoring shows reduced 504s.
03/12 - Created platform ticket INT-4125 to standardize proxy buffer-size across fleet and add ALB/proxy timeout alignment runbook.
Follow-up: Need product sign-off for automatic HTTP/1.1 fallback behavior for multipart uploads; file: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/5242
